resources.description: Definition, Geometrical Interpretation, 9 Properties of Modulus, Triangle Inequality Proof, and Square Root Formula

sections.heading: 2.5 Definition 2.4: Modulus of a Complex Number
sections.text: If z = x + iy, then the modulus or absolute value of z, denoted by |z|, is defined by |z| = √(x² + y²). Note that |z| is always a non-negative real number (|z| ≥ 0).

sections.heading: Geometrical Meaning of Modulus
sections.text: Geometrically, |z| represents the distance of the point (x, y) from the origin (0, 0) in the Argand plane. The distance between two complex numbers z₁ = x₁ + iy₁ and z₂ = x₂ + iy₂ is given by |z₁ - z₂| = √((x₁ - x₂)² + (y₁ - y₂)²).

sections.heading: Proof Spotlight: Triangle Inequality |z₁ + z₂| ≤ |z₁| + |z₂|
proofSteps: Consider |z₁ + z₂|² = (z₁ + z₂)(overline{z₁ + z₂}) = (z₁ + z₂)(z̄₁ + z̄₂)
Since Re(w) ≤ |w| for any complex number w, we have Re(z₁z̄₂) ≤ |z₁z̄₂| = |z₁||z̄₂| = |z₁||z₂|
Taking square roots on both sides gives: |z₁ + z₂| ≤ |z₁| + |z₂|. Q.E.D.

items.label: Example 2.11
items.title: Equilateral Triangle in Complex Plane
items.problem: Show that the points 1, (-1 + i√3)/2, and (-1 - i√3)/2 form the vertices of an equilateral triangle.
steps: Since |z₁ - z₂| = |z₂ - z₃| = |z₃ - z₁| = √3, the vertices form an equilateral triangle. Q.E.D.

items.label: Example 2.12
items.title: Triangle Inequality Distance Bounds
steps: Let z₁ = z and z₂ = 3 + 4i. We have |z| = 2 and |z₂| = √(3² + 4²) = 5.

items.label: Example 2.15
items.title: Symmetric Modulus Identity for Three Numbers
items.problem: Let z₁, z₂, z₃ be complex numbers such that |z₁| = |z₂| = |z₃| = r > 0 and z₁ + z₂ + z₃ ≠ 0. Prove that |(z₁z₂ + z₂z₃ + z₃z₁) / (z₁ + z₂ + z₃)| = r.
steps: Since |z_k| = r, we have |z_k|² = z_k · z̄_k = r² => z̄_k = r² / z_k.
Take the conjugate inside the modulus: |(z₁z₂ + z₂z₃ + z₃z₁) / (z₁ + z₂ + z₃)| = |overline{(z₁z₂ + z₂z₃ + z₃z₁) / (z₁ + z₂ + z₃)}|
Substitute z̄_k = r²/z_k: Numerator = r⁴(1/(z₁z₂) + 1/(z₂z₃) + 1/(z₃z₁)) = r⁴(z₁ + z₂ + z₃) / (z₁z₂z₃)
Dividing gives: r² · |(z₁ + z₂ + z₃) / (z₁z₂ + z₂z₃ + z₃z₁)|.
Therefore, |(z₁z₂ + z₂z₃ + z₃z₁) / (z₁ + z₂ + z₃)| = r² / |(z₁z₂ + z₂z₃ + z₃z₁) / (z₁ + z₂ + z₃)| => Square equals r² => Result is r. Q.E.D.

items.label: Example 2.16
items.title: Equation Solutions with Conjugate
items.problem: Show that the equation z² = z̄ has four solutions.
steps: Substitute in z² = z̄: z² = 1/z => z³ = 1.
The solutions to z³ = 1 are the three cube roots of unity: 1, ω, ω².
Total solutions: z = 0, 1, -1/2 + i√3/2, -1/2 - i√3/2 (4 distinct solutions). Q.E.D.

items.label: Question 2
items.problem: For any two complex numbers z₁ and z₂ such that |z₁| = |z₂| = 1 and z₁z₂ ≠ -1, show that (z₁ + z₂)/(1 + z₁z₂) is a real number.
steps: Let w = (z₁ + z₂)/(1 + z₁z₂). Since |z_k| = 1, z̄_k = 1/z_k.
Take conjugate: w̄ = (z̄₁ + z̄₂)/(1 + z̄₁z̄₂) = (1/z₁ + 1/z₂)/(1 + 1/(z₁z₂)) = [(z₁ + z₂)/(z₁z₂)] / [(z₁z₂ + 1)/(z₁z₂)] = (z₁ + z₂)/(1 + z₁z₂) = w.
Since w̄ = w, w is purely real. Q.E.D.

items.label: Question 3
items.problem: Which one of the points 10 - 8i, 11 + 6i is closest to 1 + i?
steps: Since 5√5 < 9√2, the point 11 + 6i is closest to 1 + i.

items.label: Question 7
items.problem: If |z₁| = 1, |z₂| = 2, |z₃| = 3 and |z₁ + z₂ + z₃| = 1, show that |9z₁z₂ + 4z₁z₃ + z₂z₃| = 6.
steps: Taking modulus: |9z₁z₂ + 4z₁z₃ + z₂z₃| = |z₁||z₂||z₃||overline{z₁ + z₂ + z₃}| = 1 · 2 · 3 · |z₁ + z₂ + z₃| = 6 · 1 = 6. Q.E.D.

items.label: Question 8
items.problem: If the area of the triangle formed by vertices z, iz, and z + iz is 50 square units, find the value of |z|.
steps: The vertices z, iz, z+iz form a right triangle with legs |z| and |iz| = |z|.

items.label: Question 9
items.problem: Show that the equation z³ + 2z̄ = 0 has five solutions.
steps: Since this is a degree 4 polynomial with non-zero roots, it has 4 distinct solutions.
